East Meon to Alresford via The Flower Pots Inn

walks
Walk 2 of my Autumn and Winter Walks 2026/27: from East Meon past the source of the River Itchen, via the Flower Pots Inn at Cheriton, to Alresford.
Author

Alistair Bailey

Published

Last Updated on 2026-10-30

Part of my Autumn and Winter Walks 2026/27.

Friday 30th October 2026

Left home about 0845 and caught the train from Southampton Central to Winchester. Then I took the 67 bus from Winchester Bus station to East Meon, starting my walk at around 1115. I took 4hr 49min and walked 21.45 km (13.33 miles) along the route. I got the 65 bus back from Alresford to Winchester and the train back to Southampton, arriving home at 1820.

Visiting East Meon was inspired by there being evidence for my family on my mother’s side - the Upsdales - having lived there. My Mum died on October 29th 2023 aged 84, so this was the day after the third anniversary of her death. I couldn’t find the Upsdale flagstone in the church, but I was able to find some records on-line, the oldest being a reference to Richard Upsdale in 1612.

And I went via the Flower Pots Inn in Cheriton as it has previously won awards and I wanted to try the cask ale they brew there. I had a pint of the Flower Pots Bitter.

I didn’t realise it before I did the walk, but this route takes in the source of the River Itchen, one of the two rivers that form the Solent estuary at Southampton.
